habitat: Hard bottoms, kelp beds, rocky reefs and wrecks, from inshore waters down to about 200 m; DORIS gives a preferred zone of 10-25 m for divers' sightings. uncertain: The identity is unsettled; I chose D. cadenati, but this needs a decision. Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes (D. sargus restricted to the Mediterranean and Black Sea; D. cadenati 'Bay of Biscay south to Senegal'), WoRMS (D. cadenati accepted), DORIS and the Andalusian catalogue (Atlantic subspecies cadenati) all put the European Atlantic white seabream under cadenati. FishBase, however, still gives D. sargus an Atlantic range 'Brittany to Gibraltar', while giving D. cadenati 'Senegal north to ... Bay of Biscay'. Béarez et al. 2017 (French checklist) lists D. sargus as the French species and flags D. cadenati as a rare non-indigenous species. Carneiro 2014 lists both subspecies for mainland Portugal. Most regional data (Veiga 2010, Bañón 2010 via FishBase, AZTI, French size rules) are filed under the name D. sargus, so regional statuses mix both names. FishBase's English name 'Moroccan white seabream' is little used; in practice this fish is the 'white seabream', 'sargo' or 'sar'. The Spanish 'Sargo' and Portuguese 'Sargo-legítimo' are taken from sources applying them to the Atlantic form (DORIS gives Spanish 'Sargo marroquí'). The usual depth of 0-50 m comes from the Andalusian 'rarely below 50 m'; the 150 m maximum is from FishBase.

cadiz.basis: Rodríguez-García et al. 2024, surf zone of Gulf of Cádiz beaches (https://rodin.uca.es/handle/10498/33592); Junta de Andalucía: more abundant in the Atlantic, Conil de la Frontera lands 52% of the Andalusian catch (https://www.juntadeandalucia.es/export/drupaljda/Especies_Pesquera_baja.pdf).

identification: Shaped like the European seabass but smaller and chubbier
Bluish back with black spots extending onto the flanks
Larger eye, larger scales and stronger opercular spines than the European seabass
Vomerine teeth form an anchor-shaped patch (a band in D. labrax)
similar: European seabass (Dicentrarchus labrax): no black spots on adults, slimmer, vomerine teeth in a band (Junta de Andalucía)
anglingMethods: Recorded in recreational shore-angling catches on the south and southwest coast of Portugal (Veiga et al. 2010, via FishBase: https://www.fishbase.se/country/CountrySummary.php?id=408&ctry=Portugal&genusname=Dicentrarchus&speciesname=punctatus&vc_code=620&speccode=394)
Trolling ('curricán') is among the Andalusian gears, along with trawl, gillnet and longline (Junta de Andalucía catalogue)
conservation: IUCN Least Concern (assessed 2014, per FishBase). France, recreational fishing in the North Sea, Channel and Atlantic: 'Bar moucheté' minimum size 30 cm (arrêté of 26 Oct 2012, version of 18 Mar 2022).

sources.title: Rodríguez-García et al. 2024, D. punctatus and D. labrax in the Gulf of Cádiz surf zone

uncertain: There is no DORIS fiche. FishBase gives depth only as '30 - ?', which conflicts with the Andalusian 2-15 m and the surf-zone data, so depth range is left null. French name: the FAO name is 'Bar tacheté'; the regulation and FishBase France use 'Bar moucheté'. Status for Biscay, Cantabria and Galicia lacks regional sources. Synonyms (e.g. Sciaena punctata Bloch, 1792) appeared only in search snippets of the FNAM name pages, so the list is left empty.

habitat: Oceanic and coastal waters over the continental shelf from the surface to about 200 m, most often along surf beaches and rocky headlands. Juveniles grow in coastal brackish nurseries; adults enter estuaries but not far.

size.maxNote: FishBase: max 130 cm TL, common 60 cm TL, max published weight 14.4 kg. DORIS: commonly 20-60 cm. Junta de Andalucía: catches usually 40-60 cm. A 76 cm TL fish was caught in Galicia in 2007.

diet: Voracious predator of schooling fish (mullets, mackerel, sardines, anchovies), plus crustaceans and cephalopods.
behaviour: Adults in loose groups attacking fish schools, reputedly killing more than they eat; juveniles school near shore. Bites when handled. Migrates to warmer water in winter and cooler water in summer. Gonochoric.
seasonal: Junta de Andalucía: the Andalusian fishery peaks July-September (99% of landings on the South Atlantic coast); spawning July-September when water exceeds 25 C. FishBase: seasonal migrations between warmer winter and cooler summer waters.

gironde.basis: No Gironde record found. Range begins in Portugal (FishBase, DORIS); Quéro et al. 1998 counted it among tropical-affinity fishes unknown north of Portugal before 1950, with 2 later records along European Atlantic coasts (https://archimer.ifremer.fr/doc/00254/36543/35085.pdf).

biscay.basis: Quéro et al. 1998: 2 records north of Portugal, with shelf records concentrated in the southern Bay of Biscay (https://archimer.ifremer.fr/doc/00254/36543/35085.pdf); peche.com says it is now also found in the Golfe de Gascogne (https://www.peche.com/article/38392/le-tassergal-un-poisson-de-plus-en-plus-abondant-pour-les-pecheurs-a-la-recherche-de-sensations-fortes).

cantabria.basis: No Cantabrian record found; north of the range given by FishBase/DORIS (Portugal southward).

galicia.basis: FishBase Spain: 'A specimen was caught 76 cm TL on 3 June 2007 in Portosin, Galicia' (Bañón et al. 2010) (https://www.fishbase.se/country/CountrySummary.php?id=378&ctry=Spain&genusname=Pomatomus&speciesname=saltatrix&vc_code=724&speccode=364).

portugal.basis: FishBase 'Portugal to South Africa' (https://www.fishbase.se/summary/Pomatomus-saltatrix.html); DORIS: north-east Atlantic sub-population from mainland Portugal to Senegal; Carneiro 2014 mainland ('Anchova'). Seasonality in Portugal not documented.

cadiz.basis: Junta de Andalucía: more abundant on the South Atlantic coast (El Puerto de Santa María and Bonanza land 94%), with a strong July-September peak (https://www.juntadeandalucia.es/export/drupaljda/Especies_Pesquera_baja.pdf).

identification: Fusiform, compressed, silvery body with grey-green back
Black blotch at the pectoral-fin base (larger in young fish)
Large oblique mouth with sharp cutting teeth; lower jaw projecting
Forked caudal; first dorsal short (7-8 spines), second dorsal and anal long and similar
similar: Greater amberjack (Seriola dumerili): less forked tail with thicker lobes, dark bar through the eye (fades in adults) (DORIS)
Leerfish (Lichia amia): deeper body, less visible scales, much more sinuous lateral line, taller fins (DORIS)
Young European seabass: rounder body, less developed caudal (DORIS)
anglingMethods: Lure fishing (surface lures, casting jigs) and live-bait fishing; handle with care because of its teeth (https://www.peche.com/article/38392/le-tassergal-un-poisson-de-plus-en-plus-abondant-pour-les-pecheurs-a-la-recherche-de-sensations-fortes)
FishBase describes it as a popular gamefish (https://www.fishbase.se/summary/Pomatomus-saltatrix.html)
conservation: IUCN Vulnerable (A2bd, assessed 2014 per FishBase; DORIS says 2015); global decline estimated at 39-53% over three generations, attributed to commercial and recreational fishing pressure (DORIS). No minimum size found for the study area.

sources.title: Quéro, Du Buit & Vayne 1998, tropical fishes and warming in European Atlantic

uncertain: Spanish: the FAO name is 'Anjova'; Andalusian markets use 'anchova' (Huelva) and 'chova/ajoa' (Cádiz). Portuguese 'Anchova' (or 'Enchova') could be confused with anchovy names. Northward presence (Gironde, Biscay, Cantabria) rests on scattered records and a popular angling article; peche.com's claim that it is increasing in the Bay of Biscay was not confirmed by a scientific source. Whether it is resident or seasonal in Portugal is not documented. DORIS's 'GB' English names (tailor, elf, etc.) are mostly non-European usages.

habitat: Rocky and sandy bottoms with algal cover or seagrass, often near beaches and breakwaters. DORIS gives surface to 20 m and the Andalusian catalogue says it rarely goes deeper than 20 m; FishBase gives 5-70 m.

size.maxNote: FishBase: max 51 cm SL, common 30 cm SL. DORIS: average 30 cm, max about 50 cm. Junta de Andalucía: up to 46 cm, rarely over 30 cm in catches.

diet: Adults almost exclusively herbivorous (green algae such as Ulva, red algae, seagrass leaves); juveniles eat mainly small crustaceans.
behaviour: Schools of several dozen fish of mixed sizes, sometimes with sars. Protandric hermaphrodite (male first; sex change at about 25-28 cm), though FishBase notes conflicting reports. Flesh can cause hallucinatory poisoning (ichthyoallyeinotoxism) if the fish is not gutted promptly.
seasonal: Junta de Andalucía: Andalusian landings slightly higher in Sept-Oct and Feb-March; spawns spring and summer. DORIS: spawning in spring and autumn.

gironde.basis: Range starts in the Bay of Biscay (https://www.fishbase.se/summary/Sarpa-salpa.html); no Gironde-specific record found.

biscay.basis: FishBase and DORIS: 'golfe de Gascogne' (https://doris.ffessm.fr/Especes/Sarpa-salpa-Saupe-431); peche.com: dense schools on the Basque Atlantic coast (https://www.peche.com/article/49033/la-peche-de-la-saupe-techniques-materiel-et-conseils-pour-reussir).

cantabria.basis: AZTI sparid poster includes S. salpa (Basque 'Sabia') with Cantabrian/Asturian names; FishBase lists many Basque vernacular names (https://www.azti.es/en/news/cada-pez-cuenta-4-infografias-para-la-identificacion-de-especies-habituales-en-la-cornisa-cantabrica/).

galicia.basis: FishBase Spain: 'Found in Galicia' (Bañón et al. 2010) (https://www.fishbase.se/country/CountrySummary.php?id=218&ctry=Spain&genusname=Sarpa&speciesname=salpa&vc_code=724&speccode=204).

portugal.basis: Carneiro 2014 mainland; FishBase: in south/southwest coast shore-angling catches (https://www.fishbase.se/country/CountrySummary.php?id=218&ctry=Portugal&genusname=Sarpa&speciesname=salpa&vc_code=620&speccode=204).

cadiz.basis: Junta de Andalucía: present in all Atlantic and Mediterranean ports; called 'salema' along the Atlantic Andalusian coast (https://www.juntadeandalucia.es/export/drupaljda/Especies_Pesquera_baja.pdf).

identification: 10-12 bright yellow/golden longitudinal lines on a grey-blue body
Small black spot at the pectoral-fin base
Golden-yellow eye
Small mouth with a single row of small sharp teeth; forked caudal fin
similar: Bogue (Boops boops): slender fusiform body with a dark lateral line and black pectoral spot; feeds on plankton rather than algae (DORIS bogue fiche: https://doris.ffessm.fr/Especes/Boops-boops-Bogue-2701)
anglingMethods: Float fishing by day with a light float (4-5 g), fine hook length and small hooks or trebles; baits: bread (most effective), paste, green filamentous algae; bread groundbait brings schools up (https://www.peche.com/article/49033/la-peche-de-la-saupe-techniques-materiel-et-conseils-pour-reussir)
Recorded in recreational shore-angling catches in southern Portugal (Veiga et al. 2010, via FishBase country record)
conservation: IUCN Least Concern (assessed 2009, per FishBase). Spain, Atlantic: minimum biological size 15 cm (RD 560/1995, as listed in the Junta de Andalucía catalogue, 2001). There is no French Atlantic recreational size in the 2022 table.

sources.title: peche.com: la pêche de la saupe

uncertain: Spawning season differs: DORIS says spring and autumn; the Andalusian catalogue says spring and summer (with juveniles appearing in May-June and Oct-Nov in the Mediterranean). Depth: FishBase 5-70 m versus DORIS/Andalusia 0-20 m. The salema-versus-bogue comparison was assembled from two separate DORIS fiches, not from a single look-alike section. There is no Gironde-specific record.

habitat: Shelf and coastal waters over sand, mud, rock and seaweed, including harbours and seagrass; mid-water near the bottom by day, rising toward the surface at night. Recorded to more than 300 m.

size.maxNote: FishBase: max 40 cm TL, common 20 cm TL. DORIS: adults average 25 cm, max 36 cm.

diet: Omnivorous to planktivorous: mostly crustaceans and plankton, also plant particles and small invertebrates.
behaviour: Strongly gregarious; loose schools of up to several thousand fish that rise to the surface mainly at night. FishBase calls it a mostly protogynous hermaphrodite (with conflicting reports), while DORIS says juveniles have ovotestes and sexes separate at maturity (11-12 cm), which DORIS does not count as hermaphroditism.
seasonal: DORIS: spawning March-May in the Atlantic. Junta de Andalucía: Andalusian landings concentrated in Jan-May and October.

gironde.basis: FishBase: 'common from the Bay of Biscay to Gibraltar' (https://www.fishbase.se/summary/Boops-boops.html). No Gironde-specific record.

biscay.basis: FishBase: common from the Bay of Biscay to Gibraltar; DORIS: Scandinavia to Angola (https://doris.ffessm.fr/Especes/Boops-boops-Bogue-2701).

cantabria.basis: AZTI sparid poster includes B. boops (Basque 'Boga') with Cantabrian/Asturian names (https://www.azti.es/en/news/cada-pez-cuenta-4-infografias-para-la-identificacion-de-especies-habituales-en-la-cornisa-cantabrica/); within the 'common' range.

galicia.basis: FishBase Spain: 'Found in Galicia' (Bañón et al. 2010) (https://www.fishbase.se/country/CountrySummary.php?id=217&ctry=Spain&genusname=Boops&speciesname=boops&vc_code=724&speccode=203).

portugal.basis: FishBase: common Bay of Biscay to Gibraltar; recorded in south/southwest coast shore-angling catches (https://www.fishbase.se/country/CountrySummary.php?id=217&ctry=Portugal&genusname=Boops&speciesname=boops&vc_code=620&speccode=203); Carneiro 2014 mainland ('Boga-do-mar').

cadiz.basis: Junta de Andalucía: present in all Andalusian ports; El Puerto de Santa María is among the top ports for an approximately 800 t/yr catch (https://www.juntadeandalucia.es/export/drupaljda/Especies_Pesquera_baja.pdf).

identification: Slender fusiform body with an oval cross-section
Long dorsal fin covering more than three-quarters of the back
Black spot at the pectoral-fin base
Lateral line clearly marked by a dark colour; large eyes and small mouth
similar: Sand smelts (Atherina): smaller, with two small dorsal fins (DORIS)
Horse mackerels (Trachurus): spiny scutes along the rear lateral line (DORIS)
Sardine, herring, anchovy: small triangular dorsal fin and no dark lateral line (DORIS)
anglingMethods: Recorded in recreational shore-angling catches on the south and southwest coast of Portugal (Veiga et al. 2010, via FishBase: https://www.fishbase.se/country/CountrySummary.php?id=217&ctry=Portugal&genusname=Boops&speciesname=boops&vc_code=620&speccode=203)
FishBase lists gamefish and bait among its human uses (https://www.fishbase.se/summary/Boops-boops.html)
conservation: IUCN Least Concern (assessed 2009, per FishBase). France: minimum catch size 12 cm (DORIS; regulation not named). Spain, Atlantic: 11 cm (RD 560/1995, as listed in the Junta de Andalucía catalogue, 2001).
uncertain: Reproductive mode is contradictory (FishBase: protogynous with conflicting reports; DORIS: not hermaphrodite). FishBase rates it 'occasional' in Portugal, but that rating comes from a shore-angling survey and conflicts with FishBase's own 'common from Biscay to Gibraltar'; the latter was used. The French 12 cm figure is from DORIS without a cited regulation, and the bogue is not in the 2022 French Atlantic recreational table. Rod-and-line techniques are not documented beyond angling catch records.
